descriptors.compatibility: WLOGP as used by SwissADME; not XLOGP3, not MLOGP, not ClogP

descriptors.label: QED
descriptors.compatibility: continuous score in [0, 1]; not a pass/fail rule

descriptors.label: Synthetic accessibility
descriptors.compatibility: Ertl-Schuffenhauer, 1 (easy) to 10 (hard); ranking score, not a rule

descriptors.label: Natural-product likeness
descriptors.compatibility: Ertl-Roggo-Schuffenhauer, about -5 (synthetic) to +5 (natural-like); ranking score, neither a rule nor a classification

profiles.name: Lipinski
profiles.notes: Rule of Five. Ships with the classical policy (one violation tolerated); switch pass_policy to {"type": "all_rules"} for the strict reading. The rule indicates a higher chance of absorption or permeation problems beyond these limits; it does not assert that every molecule inside them is an oral drug. LogP here is the Wildman-Crippen estimate, not ClogP or MLOGP.

profiles.name: Veber
profiles.notes: Complements Lipinski with molecular flexibility and polar surface area. The original study associated these two criteria with a higher probability of good oral bioavailability in its own experimental set.
